questions.question: Describe fossil fuel, list the types of fossil fuels and explain the process of it's formation.
questions.solution_html:
• Petroleum, coal, and natural gas are called fossil fuels -they formed from the remains of plants and
  • animals ((1 mark))
  • Coal is an organic sedimentary rock made up of decomposed and compacted plant remains. When
  • plants die, their remains usually decompose by reaction with oxygen. In a reducing environment
  • undecayed or partially decayed plant remains form peat. As peat is buried and compacted by overlying
  • sediments, it converts to coal, a hard, black, combustible rock, Plant matter is composed mainly of
  • carbon, hydro gen, and oxygen and contains large amounts of water. During burial, rising pressure
  • expels the water and chemical reactions release most of the hydrogen and oxygen, and the proportion of
  • carbon increases. The result is coal, a combustible rock composed mainly of carbon ((3 marks)).
  • Petroleum /crude oil is a fossil fuel having chemistry -HC+ NSO compounds. Streams carry organic
  • matter from decaying land plants and animals to the sea and to some large lakes, and deposit it with mud
  • in shallow coastal waters. Marine plants and animals die and settle to the sea floor, adding more organic
  • matter to the mud. Younger sediment then buries this organic-rich mud. Rising temperature and pressure
  • resulting from burial convert the mud to shale. At the same time, the elevated temperature and pressure
  • convert the organic matter to liquid petroleum that is finely dispersed in the rock. The activity of bacteria
  • may enhance the process. Typically, petroleum forms in the temperature range from 50 to 100ºC. At
  • temperatures above about 100ºC, oil begins to convert to natural gas ((3 marks)).
questions.final_answer: temperatures above about 100ºC, oil begins to convert to natural gas ()
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) Regular Exam Sem 1, Nov 2024

questions.question: Describe how the Lithosphere, Biosphere, and Hydrosphere interact to support / life.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition of lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere ((1 mark))
  • Lithosphere–Biosphere interaction: The lithosphere provides soil, minerals, and nutrients that
  • support plant growth (producers). Ecosystem formation: Plants, animals, and decomposers in the
  • biosphere depend on lithospheric soil and environment to form ecosystems such as forests, deserts
  • ponds, and marine systems ((2 marks)).
  • Hydrosphere–Biosphere interaction: The hydrosphere provides water required for photosynthesis
  • respiration, and survival of all living organisms. Aquatic ecosystems support diverse life forms.
  • Role of the water cycle ((2 marks))
  • Lithosphere–Hydrosphere interaction: Water infiltrates the lithosphere to form groundwater; rock
  • weathering by water releases nutrients that plants absorb ((1 mark)).
  • Combined effect supporting life: Nutrients from lithosphere + water from hydrosphere + living
  • organisms in biosphere together maintain food chains, nutrient cycles, and balanced ecosystems
  • necessary for life ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: necessary for life ()
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Describe how the Lithosphere, Biosphere, and Hydrosphere interact to support / life.
questions.solution_html:
• Definition of lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere ((1 mark))
  • Lithosphere–Biosphere interaction: The lithosphere provides soil, minerals, and nutrients that
  • support plant growth (producers). Ecosystem formation: Plants, animals, and decomposers in the
  • biosphere depend on lithospheric soil and environment to form ecosystems such as forests, deserts
  • ponds, and marine systems ((2 marks)).
  • Hydrosphere–Biosphere interaction: The hydrosphere provides water required for photosynthesis
  • respiration, and survival of all living organisms. Aquatic ecosystems support diverse life forms.
  • Role of the water cycle ((2 marks))
  • Lithosphere–Hydrosphere interaction: Water infiltrates the lithosphere to form groundwater; rock
  • weathering by water releases nutrients that plants absorb ((1 mark)).
  • Combined effect supporting life: Nutrients from lithosphere + water from hydrosphere + living
  • organisms in biosphere together maintain food chains, nutrient cycles, and balanced ecosystems
  • necessary for life ((1 mark))
questions.final_answer: necessary for life ()
